topics.concept: A good user story follows the role, goal, benefit template: as a role I want a goal so that I get a benefit. The format forces the writer to name who benefits and why, not just what to build. A writer tool scaffolds this structure and scores stories on clarity, testability, and independence.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded story drafts from feature ideas, scores each against story-quality rules, and rewrites weak stories into the standard template.
topics.name: User Story Writer
topics.real_world_use: Agile teams draft stories in this format so developers understand the user value behind each ticket.

topics.concept: Acceptance criteria turn a story into a contract: given a context, when an action happens, then an outcome follows. A checker validates that each criterion is specific, measurable, and testable, rejecting vague words like fast or user-friendly. Clear criteria end most arguments about whether a story is done.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded backlog of stories with criteria of varying quality, scores each criterion on specificity and testability, and flags vague phrasing with rewrites.
topics.name: Acceptance Criteria Checker
topics.real_world_use: QA engineers use acceptance criteria as the basis for test cases and sign-off.

topics.concept: A project glossary defines every domain term once, in plain language, so business and engineering mean the same thing by the same word. Ambiguous terms are the quiet source of most requirement defects. The builder extracts candidate terms from requirement text and drafts definitions for review.
topics.data_idea: Scans seeded requirement documents for repeated domain terms, proposes definitions, and flags terms used with conflicting meanings.

key_params.min_occurrences: mentions needed to qualify as a term

topics.name: Project Glossary Builder
topics.real_world_use: Business analysts maintain glossaries to prevent terminology drift across teams.

topics.concept: Tagging every requirement with a unique ID makes it traceable through design, code, and tests. Consistent ID schemes encode the requirement type and area, so REQ-FUNC-014 is self-describing. A tagger assigns IDs, detects duplicates, and keeps the numbering clean as scope grows.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded requirement statements across types, assigns structured IDs, and detects near-duplicate requirements by text similarity.
topics.name: Requirement ID Tagger
topics.real_world_use: Regulated projects tag requirements so auditors can trace each one to its test.

topics.concept: Large stories get split by workflow steps, business rules, data variations, or happy versus unhappy paths. Each slice must still deliver user value on its own, or the split just creates fragments. A splitting guide suggests candidate slices and checks each against the independence rule.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded epic-sized stories, proposes splits along standard patterns, and scores each slice for independent value delivery.
topics.name: Story Splitting Guide
topics.real_world_use: Scrum teams split epics in refinement so each sprint delivers something shippable.

topics.concept: A definition of done lists the exit criteria for any story: coded, tested, documented, and accepted. Without it, done means whatever the developer felt like that day. The checklist builder tailors the standard list to the project's stack and compliance needs.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded project profile with stack and compliance tags, assembles a tailored done-checklist, and audits sample stories against it.

key_params.compliance_tags: regulatory needs like audit or privacy

topics.name: Definition of Done Checklist
topics.real_world_use: Agile teams post their definition of done on the wall to make quality expectations explicit.

topics.concept: A persona card compresses a user segment into one page: name, goals, frustrations, and typical tasks. Personas keep design discussions about real humans instead of abstract users. The builder assembles cards from seeded research notes and keeps each persona anchored to observed behaviors.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded interview notes per segment, synthesizes persona cards with goals and pain points, and maps each persona to the features they care about.

key_params.traits: card fields like goals and frustrations

topics.name: Persona Card Builder
topics.real_world_use: UX teams pin persona cards in design reviews to keep user needs visible.

topics.concept: An epic-theme map groups stories under epics and epics under strategic themes, showing how daily work ladders to strategy. Orphan stories with no theme reveal work that may not matter. The mapper builds the hierarchy and flags stories that do not connect upward.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded backlog with themes, epics, and stories including orphans, builds the hierarchy, and reports coverage of themes by story count.
topics.name: Epic Theme Mapper
topics.real_world_use: Product managers use theme maps in quarterly planning to show strategy-to-execution linkage.

topics.concept: MoSCoW sorting forces every requirement into must, should, could, or will-not-have for this release. Must-haves define the minimum viable product; everything else is negotiable. The prioritizer applies the rules strictly and surfaces requirements that stakeholders labeled must but that behave like coulds.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded requirement list with stakeholder votes and effort estimates, applies MoSCoW classification rules, and flags mislabeled items for review.
topics.name: MoSCoW Prioritizer
topics.real_world_use: Release managers use MoSCoW to negotiate scope when deadlines slip.

topics.concept: A traceability matrix links each requirement to its design element, code module, and test case in both directions. Forward tracing proves every requirement is built; backward tracing proves nothing extra was built. Gaps in the matrix are untested requirements or untestable code.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded requirements, design items, and tests with partial links, builds the matrix, and reports orphan requirements and untested links.
topics.name: Traceability Matrix Builder
topics.real_world_use: Safety-critical projects maintain traceability matrices for certification audits.

topics.concept: A business requirements document opens with objectives, then scope, stakeholders, requirements, and constraints in a standard outline. The outline is the skeleton that keeps a BRD from becoming a rambling wish list. A generator drafts the full outline from a project brief and leaves the detail sections to fill in.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded project briefs with objectives and constraints, generates the complete BRD outline with section prompts, and checks coverage of standard sections.
topics.name: BRD Outline Generator
topics.real_world_use: Business analysts start BRDs from outlines to get stakeholder sign-off on structure before writing.

topics.concept: A software requirements specification organizes requirements by feature with interfaces, performance targets, and constraints per section. Consistency across sections is what separates an SRS from a pile of notes. The builder assembles sections from tagged requirements and checks cross-references.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded feature requirements with interface and performance details, assembles them into SRS sections, and validates cross-reference integrity.
topics.name: SRS Section Builder
topics.real_world_use: Enterprise vendors write SRS documents as the contractual basis for custom builds.

topics.concept: A use case describes an actor's goal, the main success path, and the extensions for everything that can go wrong. Enumerating the failure paths is where the real requirements hide. The writer scaffolds actors, preconditions, steps, and extensions into the classic format.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded actor-goal pairs, drafts main success scenarios plus extension paths, and checks that every extension resolves or fails safely.
topics.name: Use Case Writer
topics.real_world_use: Systems analysts write use cases to capture interaction requirements before design.

topics.concept: Non-functional requirements cover performance, security, reliability, and usability: the qualities that make software acceptable rather than just functional. They must be measurable, like response under two seconds at peak load, or they are unenforceable. A cataloger collects them by quality attribute and attaches a metric to each.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded quality-attribute targets, drafts measurable NFR statements per attribute, and flags NFRs that lack a quantifiable metric.

key_params.attributes: quality attributes like performance and security

topics.name: NFR Cataloger
topics.real_world_use: Architects sign off on NFR catalogs before design so qualities are engineered in.

topics.concept: A change request log records every scope change with its reason, impact estimate, and approval decision. It is the audit trail that explains why the plan moved. The log links each change to affected requirements so nothing changes silently.
topics.data_idea: Simulates a seeded stream of change requests with impacts and decisions, maintains the log, and reports scope creep as approved change volume over time.
topics.name: Change Request Log
topics.real_world_use: Project managers defend schedules with change logs that quantify approved scope growth.

topics.concept: Backlog refinement scoring ranks stories by value, effort, and risk so the team always works on the best next thing. Weighted scoring beats gut feel when stakeholders disagree. The scorer combines business value, urgency, and effort into one ranked list with the reasoning visible.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded backlog with value, urgency, and effort scores, applies a weighted ranking formula, and shows how reweighting changes the order.
topics.name: Backlog Refinement Scorer
topics.real_world_use: Product owners use scoring models to make prioritization defensible in stakeholder reviews.

topics.concept: Requirements volatility measures how often requirements change after baselining: added, modified, or deleted per period. Rising volatility predicts schedule slips better than most status reports. Tracking it by area shows which parts of the scope are still churning.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded requirement baselines with change events over time, computes volatility indices per area, and correlates volatility with projected slip.
topics.name: Requirements Volatility Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Program managers watch volatility to decide when scope is stable enough to commit to dates.

topics.concept: Requirements depend on each other, and a dependency graph makes those links explicit: changing one ripples to its neighbors. Cycles in the graph signal contradictory or circular requirements. The analyzer builds the graph, finds cycles, and computes the blast radius of any proposed change.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded requirements with dependency links including a planted cycle, builds the graph, detects cycles, and computes impacted sets for sample changes.
topics.name: Requirement Dependency Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Systems engineers use dependency analysis to scope the true cost of a change request.

topics.concept: Conflicting requirements demand incompatible things, like maximum security with zero login friction. A detector compares constraints across requirements for logical contradictions and resource over-allocation. Catching conflicts in text is far cheaper than discovering them in testing.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded requirements with planted contradictions in constraints and targets, applies contradiction rules, and reports each conflict with the offending pair.
topics.name: Requirement Conflict Detector
topics.real_world_use: Analysts run conflict checks before baselining to avoid building impossible specifications.

topics.concept: The Kano model classifies features as basic expectations, performance satisfiers, or delighters that surprise. Basics cause anger when missing but no joy when present; delighters do the opposite. Classifying the backlog this way guides where to invest for differentiation versus table stakes.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded survey responses to functional and dysfunctional questions per feature, classifies each into Kano categories, and maps the backlog mix.
topics.name: Kano Feature Classifier
topics.real_world_use: Product teams use Kano results to balance must-have quality against differentiating features.

topics.concept: Story point calibration aligns the team's sense of a point by comparing estimates against actuals over time. Systematic over- or under-estimation shows up as a consistent ratio, not random noise. The calibrator tracks the ratio per estimator and suggests adjustments that make planning honest.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded estimates and actuals per team member with planted biases, computes calibration ratios, and recommends adjusted planning factors.
topics.name: Story Point Calibrator
topics.real_world_use: Scrum masters use calibration data to improve sprint planning accuracy.

topics.concept: A compliance trace audit verifies that every regulatory requirement maps to an implemented control and a passing test. Missing links are audit findings waiting to happen. The auditor walks the full chain from regulation to evidence and reports gaps with severity.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded regulation-to-control-to-test chains with planted gaps, audits the chains, and reports missing links ranked by severity.
topics.name: Compliance Trace Auditor
topics.real_world_use: Compliance officers run trace audits before external assessments to find gaps early.

topics.concept: Impact analysis answers what breaks if a requirement changes: dependent requirements, design elements, tests, and schedule. It turns a casual change request into a priced decision. The analyzer traverses the traceability graph from the changed node and totals the blast radius.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded traceability graph, applies sample requirement changes, traverses impacted nodes, and prices the impact in effort and schedule.
topics.name: Change Impact Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Change control boards require impact analysis before approving scope changes.

topics.concept: Baselining freezes requirements at a milestone, and a diff report shows exactly what moved since the last baseline: added, removed, and modified items with their history. It is the honest record of scope evolution. The reporter computes the diff and summarizes the direction and magnitude of change.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded requirement versions across two baselines with edits, computes the add-remove-modify diff, and summarizes scope drift by area.
topics.name: Baseline Diff Reporter
topics.real_world_use: Project sponsors review baseline diffs to approve or challenge scope movement.
